content:
Siri AI is a major upgrade for Apple's assistant, and is now available on iOS 27. I've noticed a standout difference between Siri AI and other AI assistants — and it's a good one.

The new Siri in iOS 27 doesn't pretend to be human, which sets it completely apart from other AI chatbots.

I've been using Siri AI for nearly four months since the first beta of iOS 27 launched. Overall, Siri AI has met all of my expectations.

The new Siri is far better than the old one, finally delivering on the original promise of providing a truly capable assistant for Apple devices.

I have to admit, if you need the most cutting-edge, most powerful AI tools on the market, competitors like ChatGPT, Claude, and Google Gemini may be better suited for you.

However, after using Siri AI and comparing it with those third-party tools, I discovered a key difference that makes me prefer Siri even more.

Unlike other AI chatbots, Siri doesn't pretend to be human.

It doesn't go on at length, mimic human personality, or try to build a personal relationship with you.

Siri is practical and smart — it does whatever you ask it to do. But the way it responds clearly shows that it's a tool, not a person. It frequently reminds you that it's AI and could make mistakes. It also doesn't pretend to develop any kind of relationship with you.

On the other hand, ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are full of personality and subjective opinions, showing a more human-like tendency — but to me, that feels very fake.

I know some users enjoy that 'humanised' approach. But I'd rather have AI assistants do their job well, rather than pretending to be something they're not.

AI is changing the world. But AI chatbots are tools, not people. I really appreciate that Apple understands this and has designed the new Siri accordingly.

How 'human-like' do you think AI assistants should be? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
